set.approach: The buttress sits deep in the Clark Range backcountry, and the walk in is long. One way starts at Happy Isles and runs up Little Yosemite Valley past Merced Lake; the other leaves Tuolumne Meadows up Rafferty Creek, passes Vogelsang High Sierra Camp and drops to the Merced Lake ranger station. From there go upstream to the junction with the Grey Peak Fork, cross the Merced River, and follow the northwest bank of the fork, where traces of an old cavalry trail help. A granite bench on the way makes a good camp, and Obelisk Lake is another possible base. The buttress comes into view through the trees on the right; take the easiest ground to its foot. The route climbs the left side, starting in the obvious set of right-facing corners that sweep up to a large sandy ledge.
set.descent_text: From the last pitch, scramble up to the crest of the ridge above the buttress. Third- and fourth-class scrambling then leads down to talus, which you follow back to the base of the route.

review.notes: Area page gives the approach; route page gives start and the scramble-off. Numbers left out.

set.approach: Starting from Humber Park, follow the Tahquitz north face trail until it aims at the north face, then peel off to the left on a faint track heading for the dry wash beneath the Devil's Staircase, continuing till Indian Buttress is directly overhead. Keep going up and left past cairns to the foot of the Altar on its right-hand side, leave your packs, and walk right along the base of the west face to the start. The route begins just below the War Bonnet Tower, a little past the Paisley Buttress, beside a tall skinny pine and under a series of stacked flakes.
set.descent_text: From the ridge top above the last pitch, you can move left along the ridge and finish the last pitches of the Altar, or pass beneath the big boulder there and hike down the east side.

review.notes: Route page states approach variant and both ways off the top.

set.approach: Walk the Tahquitz north face trail, then go on toward Indian Buttress along faint paths that hug the creek. Once you are almost beneath Indian Buttress, cross the creek and climb the ravine to the foot of the Amphitheater itself, at the right-hand end of the First Terrace. The cirque as a whole is reached by way of the Strawberry Creek drainage. The route starts in a chimney and layback section that leads to a big pine tree.
set.descent_text: From the top of the last pitch, hike down to the Devil's Slide trail, which returns to Humber Park.

review.notes: Route page gives approach and the walk-down.

set.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. The route is on the right side of the left-hand of the two formations above Arctic Lakes and begins on orange, featured rock.
set.descent_text: Travel west from the summit, then turn south and descend back to the lakes.

review.notes: Wall approach from area page; start and descent from route page.

set.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. To find the start, look for the largest double-roof feature on the wall, then follow the single vertical crack at the left edge of those roofs down to the ground. The route starts in a flaky corner system there.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the left from the top and follow the sandy slope back down.

set.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. This route is not on the main wall. It is on a smaller wall just above the lower camp below Arctic Lake Wall. Find the second large boulder to the right of a black streak; a clean crack splits the face above, with a stem-box chimney in the middle.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the right from the top.

set.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. Locate the second-largest corner system from the east (right) side of the face and trace a line down to the ledge at its base, where the route starts.
set.descent_text: The wall descends by a class 2 walk-off. From the summit, head southwest toward the western ridge until you reach the broad gully on the left flank of the peak, then follow it down to your packs or camp.

review.notes: Route page: location. Area page: wall descent.

set.approach: Bat Rock is a crag on the north side of Highway 155, west of Wofford Heights, and the hike up to it is steep. The route starts at the base of the far right side of the south face, at a natural mineral stain shaped like the Roman numeral nine.

review.notes: Route page: start and rappel; area page: access.

set.approach: Bat Rock is a crag on the north side of Highway 155, west of Wofford Heights, and the hike up to it is steep. Seen from the road, the line runs up the crack system on the rock's left side.

review.notes: Route and area pages; no descent source.

set.approach: The Bear's Behind is a south-facing wall a short, easy hike northwest of The Egg. Hairy Bear starts in the center of the south face, climbs the face to a right-slanting crack, and joins the route Sunkiss near the top.
Take the trail from Lake Sabrina to Blue Lake, then expect a stretch of bushwhacking and scrambling to reach the crag on the south side of the lake. The dihedral is on the south side of Blue Lake.

review.notes: Route and area pages; no descent for this line.

set.approach: Take the trail from Lake Sabrina to Blue Lake, then expect a stretch of bushwhacking and scrambling to reach the crag on the south side of the lake. The crack is on the southeast side of the lake: weave through the boulder tier a level above the water until a hidden grassy meadow opens up. The crack is obvious from there.

Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. The route is the obvious overhanging crack and dihedral to the left of the tree of the day.

Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Crystal Licker starts from a small block that lets you reach the first holds, and climbs through underclings to a crystal band.

Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Enemy Mine is on the right side of the buttress, where grey bolts mark an arching flake that faces left and is climbed by laybacking.

Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. The route starts just off the trail. The variation start begins up the bolted route immediately to its left, then cuts right to a stance below the anchor of Mine's Eye.

review.notes: Route page states rappelling the route; rope count left out.

set.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Mine Over Matter lies a little higher on the slope than the Mine in the Sky start. A built-up platform marks the foot of a finger crack that leads into a bolted face.

Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Never Mined starts at a wide crack just to the right of Mine Over Matter.

Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Nutter Butter starts a little right of the Mine in the Sky variation start and shares its first two bolts with I Me Mine.
set.descent_text: Lower from the anchor hardware at the top.

review.notes: Route page states lowering from the anchor.

set.approach: From Road's End in Kings Canyon, where the camping permit is issued, hike east on the trail to a good camp just past Charlotte Creek, then continue a short way until the wall is visible on the left. Use the approach for the route The Emperor, since Hanshi shares that route's first pitch.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the top down to the level where Hanshi joins What's Up Bubb, then follow that route's rappels to the base.

review.notes: Route page gives approach reference and rappel descent.

set.approach: From Road's End in Kings Canyon, hike east on the trail to the good camp just past Charlotte Creek. From camp, continue a short distance to a climbers' trail and follow the cairns up into a steep dry streambed. Near its top, bear left into the main gully that ends the right side of the whole wall. The route climbs the first few pitches of Ikigai before splitting off toward the golden headwall.

From the circular parking area, walk west and slightly uphill for a short hike to the formation. The route climbs a thin crack to a ledge on the right side of the main face, then the featured face above, to a bolted anchor.

Burnt Granola is the squarish cliff just north of where Highway 178 meets Chimney Peak Road. Park where Chimney Peak Road heads east under the cliff and walk a short way to the base. The route follows the center of the face to two obvious water cracks.

The pinnacles are roadside, midway between Low Maintenance Rock and High Profile Pinnacle, north of Forest Road 2N13. Park along the road and walk a short distance north. The route is a hand-sized crack splitting the south face of the left pinnacle.

The pinnacles are roadside, midway between Low Maintenance Rock and High Profile Pinnacle, north of Forest Road 2N13. Park along the road and walk a short distance north. The route follows a hand crack on the east face of the right pinnacle.

Head up the John Muir Trail toward Cathedral Lakes. After the second set of switchbacks, when the tip of the wall first shows, keep walking until the trail crosses the creek and climbs another set of switchbacks, then leave the trail and walk cross-country straight at the wall; the going is open, with no thick brush. The route is a direct line toward the top of the wall, and the corner that dominates the fourth pitch is the feature to aim for.

From the South Lake trailhead, take the Bishop Pass trail to Le Conte Canyon and turn south on the John Muir Trail along the Middle Fork of the Kings River for a couple of miles. Find a crossing of the river above the mouth of Ladder Creek, then work up the small side valley toward the Citadel, getting over Ladder Creek where it is easy. The east arete is the long east-facing ridge. To find the start, watch for a clean corner facing left, low on the ridge by the final bushes and trees.
